questions.question:
In the following question, select the related number from the given alternatives.

**553 : 551 ∷ 447 : ?**
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

First Term - 2 = Second Term

553 - 2 = 551

Similarly,

447 - 2 = 445

Hence, 445 is the right answer.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd word pair from the given alternatives.

questions.question: In the following question, four number pairs are given. The number on left side of (–) is related to the number of the right side of (–) with some Logic/Rule/Relation. Three are similar on basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

**(First Number)² = Second Number**

Applying the above logic to each option, we get

(9)² = 81

(8)² = 64

(6)² = 36

**(7)² = 49 ≠ 47**

Thus, 7 – 47 is the odd one out.

Hence, the correct answer is, **"7 – 47".**

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

**XPK, VNJ, TLH, RJE, ?**
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

First letter of each word: X - 2 = V; V - 2 = T; T - 2 = R; R - 2 = **P**

Second letter of each word: P - 2 = N; N - 2 = L; L - 2 = J; J - 2 = **H**

Third letter of each word: K - 1 = J; J - 2 = H; H - 3 = E; E - 4 = **A**

Hence, ‘PHA’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a row of swimmers Manish, is 23rd from the left end. Ramesh is 11 ranks to the left of Manish. If Ramesh is 16th from right end, then how many swimmers are there in this row?
questions.solution:
Manish is 23rd from the left end.

Ramesh is 11 ranks to the left of Manish. i.e. Ramesh is (23 - 11) = 12th from the left end.

Ramesh is 16th from the right end.

Total number of swimmers: 16 + 12 - 1 = 27

Hence, the correct answer is, **"27".**

4) Sour: RE**SOUR**CES, hence word can be formed.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Rise".**

questions.question: A marketing executive goes on his field work and walks 2 km North, then he turns West and walks 6 km, then he turns North and walks 7 km, and then he turns to his right and walks 6 km. Where is he now with respect to his starting position?
questions.solution:
As per the given information,

First he walks 2 km North, then he turns West and walks 6 km, then he turns North and walks 7 km, and then he turns to his right and walks 6 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4940121d13b01195720dbf0ce8be3dc7a494fe69b6ab58cca4dfc09bdf062057.png] 

So, the marketing executive is 9 km to the north from his starting position.

Hence, the correct answer is** "9 km North".**

questions.question:
In the question, two statements are given, followed by two conclusions, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

**Statement I:** All cakes are pastries

**Statement II:** Some bread are cakes

**Conclusion I:** No pastries are bread

**Conclusion II:** Some bread are pastries

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible diagram of this question is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23c7f0e167980b01199d7aaec91cd9789af386cdd04cb7d763bd6590d12fedb0.png] 

**Conclusion I:** No pastries are bread → Does not follow (As all cakes are pastries and some cakes are bread, thus some pastries will be bread.)

**Conclusion II:** Some bread are pastries → Follows (As some bread is cakes and all cakes are pastries, thus some bread will be pastries.

Thus, only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is, **"Only conclusion II follows".**

questions.question:
In the following figure, rectangle represents Chefs, circle represents Choreographers, triangle represents Divers and square represents Americans. Which set of letters represents Americans who are either Choreographers or Divers?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42aac8b970bc82def317d73a32200ffdb6a1a4c4d85fd008bc3bc2bd48af804c.png]
questions.solution:
Here,

The alphabet in the rectangle represents Chefs: A and B

Circle represents Choreographers: D, G, E and F

Triangle represents Divers: E, G, H, and I

Square represents Americans: C, E, H, D and B

The set of letters represents Americans who are either Choreographers or Divers are letters in the Square and common with the Triangle or the Circle, which is DEH.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e094a8df58f6266482c2c9dd028bc362390ef10e73f6e31c3c0c3190a52fc8d.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is **"DEH".**

questions.solution:

Second letter of each word: A + 3 = D; D + 3 = G; G + 3 = J; J + 3 =** M**

Hence, UMD is the correct answer.

questions.solution:

questions.question: A word is represented by only set of numbers as given in any one of the alternatives. The sets of numbers given in the alternatives are represented by two classes of alphabets as shown in the given two matrices. The columns and rows of Matrix-I are numbered from 0 to 4 and that of Matrix-II are numbered from 5 to 9. A letter from these matrices can be represented first by its row and next by its column, for example ‘J’ can be represented by 21, 14 etc. and ‘P’ can be represented by 95, 86 etc. Similarly, you have to identify the set for the word ‘LITE’. **Matrix I** 0 1 2 3 4 0 C C F C
questions.solution:
Applying the logic as given in the table to each option, we get

1) 14, 97, 42, 78 → J, N, D, Z

2) 22, 77, 22, 58 → F, Z, F, Q

3) 24, 79, 12, 56 → J, T, G, W

4) **20, 43, 55, 31 → L, I, T, E**

Hence, the correct answer is **‘20, 43, 55, 31’**
